stops.note: 'last', the superlative of posterus 'later', used of a child born after its father's death, as in the Roman name Postumus
an h crept in because writers misread it as post 'after' + humus 'earth, burial'
kept the mistaken h, and widened to anything that comes after death, such as a posthumous award

current_meaning: occurring or published after the death of its originator
